classification.classification_note: AddressSanitizer reports a std::vector container-overflow because `parseIdentifier()` reads one byte past the normalized `m_buffer` size while the vector still retains a larger reserved allocation.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42499530 (assimp): Container-overflow READ 1 found by fuzz target assimp_fuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42499530
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / patch.diff / arvo_workspace/vulnerable_run.log / staged vulnerable source / staged `poc` bytes
bug_description.normalized: The exact staged witness is the 543-byte file with SHA-256 `3ad20f9f69f3f27c55da45655ad591f3710d25c8e69e8bacf61e7b9735c23a7e`, beginning `Lvertexarray (attribWMO\nNumChann...`. Stage 01's saved run log shows assimp performs signature-based detection and selects the Open Game Engine Exchange importer. `OpenGEXImporter::InternReadFile()` calls `TextFileToBuffer()`, which reads the 543 attacker-controlled bytes and appends one trailing `0`, and `OpenDDLParser::setBuffer()` copies the resulting 544-byte sequence into parser-owned `m_buffer`. `parse()` immediately calls `normalizeBuffer(m_buffer)`, which removes all 30 newline bytes from this witness but preserves the appended NUL, so parsing continues with a 514-byte vector whose first header is `Lvertexarray (` and whose bytes after that `(` form a 500-byte suffix with no spaces, commas, close-property tokens, or newlines before the final NUL. `parseHeader()` parses `Lvertexarray`, sees the open-property token `(`, and `parseProperty()` then calls `parseIdentifier()` on that separator-free suffix as the first property name. Vulnerable `parseIdentifier()` uses `while (!isSeparator(*in) && !isNewLine(*in) && (in != end) && *in != Grammar::OpenPropertyToken[0] && *in != Grammar::ClosePropertyToken[0] && *in != '$')`, so it increments across every byte of the property text and also across the trailing NUL because NUL is not treated as a terminator. That advances `in` from the last valid byte to `end`, and on the next loop-condition evaluation the leftmost `*in` in `isSeparator(*in)` is read before `(in != end)` is checked. Stage 01 reproduces `AddressSanitizer: container-overflow READ of size 1` at `OpenDDLParser.cpp:535:25` in `parseIdentifier`. The staged patch fixes this exact path by reordering the loop to `while ((in != end) && ... )` and by adding sibling `in != end` guards in surrounding property parsing.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The identifier-scan loop dereferences `*in` before checking `in != end` and does not treat the appended NUL as a terminator, so a separator-free property token that reaches EOF advances `in` to `end` and makes the next condition evaluation read one byte past the vector's logical end.
root_cause.note: The staged patch changes this loop to `while ((in != end) && ... )`, preventing the dereference at `end`; the same patch also adds `in != end` guards around `parseHeader()` and `parseProperty()`.

sink.description: ASan crash site. After the loop in step 7 has advanced `in` to `end`, the next `isSeparator(*in)` read dereferences one byte past `m_buffer.size()`, producing the saved container-overflow READ of size 1.
sink.note: The saved ASan report points to `OpenDDLParser.cpp:535:25`, and the faulting address is 514 bytes inside the 544-byte allocation created by `OpenDDLParser::setBuffer()`.

tainted_value_origin.description: This normalization step removes newline bytes from the copied OpenDDL text but preserves the final NUL, creating the exact separator-free property token that later reaches `parseIdentifier()`.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The staged `poc` has 543 bytes with 30 newline bytes. After `TextFileToBuffer()` appends one `0`, `normalizeBuffer()` removes those 30 newlines and leaves a 514-byte `buffer`; after the first `(` there are 500 bytes up to the preserved NUL and none of them are space, comma, `)`, or newline separators.
tainted_value_origin.note: This transformed suffix is the attacker-derived parser state that makes the later identifier scan run off the logical end.

fine_trace.note: Source. After signature-based importer selection, this call reads the exact 543-byte witness into `buffer`; `TextFileToBuffer()` appends one trailing `0`, so the parser-side input becomes a 544-byte sequence.

`myParser.setBuffer(&buffer[0], buffer.size())` copies the full 544-byte importer buffer from step 1, including the appended NUL, into parser-owned `m_buffer`. The later `current`, `in`, and `end` pointers all refer into this copied vector.

`parse()` normalizes the copied buffer by dropping every newline byte and keeping all other bytes, including the trailing NUL. For this witness that changes the parser vector from 544 bytes to 514 bytes and concatenates the raw property text after the first `(` into a 500-byte suffix with no space, comma, `)`, or newline separators before the final NUL.

After normalization, `parse()` sets `current` to the first byte of the 514-byte vector and sets `end` one byte past its last element. The last element before `end` is the preserved NUL from step 3, so any scan that increments across that NUL arrives exactly at `end`.

Starting from `current`, `parseHeader()` first consumes the node identifier `Lvertexarray`. `lookForNextToken()` then lands on the literal `(` from the witness, so the open-property branch is taken and `in++` moves to the first property byte `a` immediately after that token.

`parseProperty()` begins at the bytes immediately after `(`. Because step 3 removed all newlines and there are no separators or close-property tokens before the trailing NUL, this `parseIdentifier()` call sees the 500-byte sequence `attribWMONumChannels...<NUL>` as one unterminated property-name candidate.

Root-cause step. Starting at the `a` from step 6, the loop finds no separator, newline, `(`, `)`, or `$` byte in the next 500 bytes. It increments across all 499 non-NUL suffix bytes and across the final NUL too, because NUL is not a terminator here, leaving `in == end` and `idLen == 500`. The missing obligation is that the condition evaluates `*in` before `(in != end)`, so arriving at `end` is not safe.

Sink. On the next loop-condition evaluation, `in` already equals `end`, but the leftmost `isSeparator(*in)` still dereferences that one-past-end pointer before the `(in != end)` term is considered. ASan reports the resulting container-overflow READ of size 1 at `OpenDDLParser.cpp:535:25`.

crash_stack.function: Assimp::Importer::ReadFileFromMemory(void const*, unsigned long, unsigned int, char const*)

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: Yes. The staged patch reorders `parseIdentifier()`'s loop guard to check `(in != end)` before dereferencing `*in`, and it adds additional `in != end` guards around the surrounding property parsing so this EOF path no longer dereferences one-past-end.

format.name: OpenGEX / OpenDDL-like text
format.contract: The verified trigger is the exact staged 543-byte `poc` with SHA-256 `3ad20f9f69f3f27c55da45655ad591f3710d25c8e69e8bacf61e7b9735c23a7e`. Signature-based detection must route it to `OpenGEXImporter`, `TextFileToBuffer()` must append the trailing NUL, and `normalizeBuffer()` must remove its 30 newline bytes so the parser starts with `Lvertexarray (` followed by a 500-byte suffix that contains no spaces, commas, `)`, or newlines before the NUL. Under that witnessed normalized layout, the first property-name parse in `parseIdentifier()` consumes the NUL, advances `in` to `end`, and the next loop-condition evaluation reads one byte past the normalized buffer. This contract is limited to that exact staged witness and the observed normalized token layout; it does not generalize to other malformed OpenDDL texts.
